title: Ellington's small band at the Kentucky Club; Wellman Braud
summary: Scott names the Ellington sidemen of the time and recalls bassist Braud's later years and the spelling of his name.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: And, well, they were recording again, recording records. And you jump right into records with Duke. And we played there, and played there quite a while. You heard of Sonny Grier, he was on drums. He lives
And Otto Hardwick and Freddy Guy. Of course, he died, he was a guitar player. And Tricky Sam was on trombone. Yeah, he died, too. And Bro, Bro was on bass.
Yeah. Well, I guess Sonny is the only one left.
Yeah, yeah. Bro was on bass. Bro -- after he left Duke, he opened up a pool parlor and I saw him one day. I used to pass by, he'd always come out and call me, and we'd stop and talk about old times.
So then he told me one day he was giving it up, he was going back to New Orleans, his home. And I shook hands with him and wished him well. Never saw him again.
Yeah, I met his brother, I think it
was. But he spelled Braut a different way. Because Wellman spelled in B-r-a-u-x. But down there they spelled it B-r-e-a-u-x.
Oh, yeah, yeah. Yes, yes, it's a French name.
Yeah. And his brother was also -- he was playing bass down there. But -- so when you went with Duke, this was '26?
When you left Fletcher and went with Duke --
And how long were you with Duke?
